One of the most profound empirical laws of star formation is the Gao-Solomon relation, a linear correlation between the star formation rate (SFR) and the dense molecular gas mass. It is puzzling how the complicated physics in star-formation results in this surprisingly simple proportionality.

In this work, we attempt to explain the Gao-Solomon relation with an alternative picture. Our main hypothesis is that the mass of the most massive core (M_core^max) in a molecular cloud is determined by the mass of the parent gravitational bound gas reservoir (M_gas^bound).
